subject.title: Transcript redaction corrupts Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signatures (AIza/LTAI false positive), causing persistent replay_invalid

question: For provider-minted signed-thinking fields, should OpenClaw preserve structurally valid opaque replay tokens even when their bytes contain credential-shaped substrings, or keep the current redaction-idempotency gate and harden patterns/replay recovery around it?
rationale: The current tests deliberately redact credential-shaped provider signature fields, but this report shows that policy can corrupt real opaque replay tokens; choosing the transcript redaction exemption boundary is security-sensitive maintainer intent.

options.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
options.body: Preserve valid opaque signatures only when route, block type, field name, and token shape prove the value is provider-owned replay metadata, then add focused repair coverage for corrupted persisted blocks.

options.title: Pattern-Only Hardening
options.body: Make vendor-prefix detectors stricter and case-sensitive while keeping the current rule that credential-looking provider signatures are redacted.

options.title: Replay Recovery Only
options.body: Leave transcript redaction unchanged and add send-side or repair stripping for ellipsis-corrupted Bedrock/Anthropic thinking blocks.

recommendation.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
recommendation.body: Preserve valid opaque signatures only when route, block type, field name, and token shape prove the value is provider-owned replay metadata, then add focused repair coverage for corrupted persisted blocks.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the merged route-bound opaque reasoning preservation behavior being reconsidered.
